splashTagline.context: Under the app name on the animated starting screen, first launch.
splashTagline.example: Plans that know how your brain works.

greetingTitle.context: Big serif hello on the first screen after the start animation.

greetingBody.context: One or two sentences under the hello, saying what the app is: a planner built around an ADHD brain and its medication.
greetingBody.example: This is a planner built around your brain and your medication, not the other way round.

accountTitle.example: First, somewhere to keep your stuff.

accountBody.context: Why an account: plans follow you to a new phone; medication is encrypted and never readable by us.
accountBody.example: An account lets your plans follow you to a new phone. Your medication is encrypted and we can’t read it.

trialTitle.context: Heading on the free-trial screen before the free plan. Must not state a trial length (Apple’s offer shows that).
trialTitle.example: Try all of it, free, for a month.

trialWhy.context: Why the trial exists: ADHD takes time to understand, and so does knowing if an app works for you. If it doesn’t, just cancel. Must end with the idea of cancelling being easy.
trialWhy.example: Because ADHD takes time to figure out, and so does knowing whether an app actually helps. If it doesn’t, just cancel.

welcomeHome.context: Small toast the first time the home page appears.

coachPriorities.context: Coach mark pointing at today’s five priorities.
coachPriorities.example: These are today’s five. Short on purpose.

coachMeds.context: Coach mark pointing at the home medication row: two medication buttons (tap to log, hold for another time) and a more button (every dose today, with Log all).
coachMeds.example: Your medication lives here. Tap one to log it. More shows the rest.

coachDots.context: Coach mark pointing at the page dots: flick up for the next page.
coachDots.example: Flick up for the next page. The dots show where you are.

coachSetup.context: Coach mark suggesting they set up medication and day types in You.
coachSetup.example: Set up your medication and day types in You. It takes about two minutes.

coachDone.context: Last coach mark; they can now explore freely.
coachDone.example: That’s the tour. Wander wherever you like.

fiveThingsEyebrow.context: Tiny uppercase label above today’s five priorities.

medsAllLogged.context: Shown under the medication row when everything due today is logged.

medsNothingDue.context: Nothing is due right now; says when the next one is.
medsNothingDue.example: Nothing due right now. Next at {time}.

medsLoggedToast.context: Toast after Log all logs some doses.

medsNone.context: No medication set up yet; invites them to add it.
medsNone.example: No medication set up yet. Add it whenever you’re ready.

nowGap.context: Headline when nothing is scheduled right now.

nowThen.context: Line under the Now card saying what’s next.

dayLineWarming.context: Status line: medication is warming up, best focus starts at time.

dayLineBest.context: Status line: in best focus until time.

dayLineLighter.context: Status line: lighter focus until time.

dayLineAfter.context: Status line: the focus window has ended for today.
dayLineAfter.example: Focus window’s done for today. Go gently.

dayLineRoutine.context: Status line on a medication-free or not-yet-logged day.

restHeadline.context: Headline: how many things are left today (count is 2 or more).

restOneLeft.context: Headline: exactly one thing left today.

restUnplaced.context: Some tasks didn’t fit without over-packing; Fix my day can help.
restUnplaced.example: {count} didn’t fit without over-packing. Fix my day can split or move it.

changeFootnote.context: Reassurance under Fix my day and Baseline buttons.
changeFootnote.example: Nothing moves until you say so. Undo is always one tap.

tinyWinsTitle.context: Headline on the page listing what they’ve finished today.

tinyWinsEmpty.context: Nothing finished yet today. Never shaming.
tinyWinsEmpty.example: Nothing ticked off yet. The day is young.

breatheIntro.context: Intro to a one-minute paced breathing page where the phone taps along.
breatheIntro.example: In for four, out for six. Your phone will tap along.

socialLine.context: Short line on the home page: a plan with other people sits at an awkward time; tap to see a suggestion.
socialLine.example: {event} is at {time}. Want to ask to move it?

socialMessage.context: Draft text message the person may send a friend asking to move a plan. Warm, casual, may joke about their own brain. They edit it before sending.
socialMessage.example: Hey {name}, any chance we could do {event} at {time} instead? My brain’s much better company then.

arrivalMorning.context: Morning greeting on the daily starting page.

arrivalAfternoon.context: Afternoon greeting on the daily starting page.

arrivalEvening.context: Evening greeting on the daily starting page.

arrivalQuestion.context: The one question on the daily starting page: how their brain feels today (answers are Low, Okay, Good).

planWeekHeadline.context: Headline: how many of the last 7 days met their baseline.

planWeekExplainer.context: Explains a baseline day: the three things that keep life moving; most weeks aren’t 7/7 and that’s fine.
planWeekExplainer.example: A day counts when your baseline is done. Most weeks aren’t seven out of seven. That’s the whole point of a baseline.

rhythmIntro.context: Under ‘Four weeks of you’: how many days counted this week.

rhythmTuneTitle.context: Headline inviting them to edit their learned patterns.

rhythmTuneBody.context: What they can change on the Patterns page; plans follow at once.
rhythmTuneBody.example: Change your focus window, how long things take, how full days get and when you eat. Plans follow straight away.

rhythmFooter.context: Footer: patterns, not scores; the data stays on the iPhone.
rhythmFooter.example: Patterns, not scores. All of this stays on your iPhone.

detailPlanDone.context: Explains the planned vs done chart: grey planned, gold done; gaps are information not failure.
detailPlanDone.example: Grey is what you planned, gold is what got done. Gaps are information, not failure.

detailBrain.context: Explains the brain weather chart; on low days the app planned a baseline day.
detailBrain.example: How you said your brain felt each morning. On low days the plan got lighter on its own.

detailHours.context: Explains the hour heatmap: each dot is an hour; brighter means more finished.
detailHours.example: Each dot is an hour. The brighter it is, the more you finished then.

detailWindow.context: Explains the learned focus curve: how often check-ins said it was working, by hours after logging; the band is certainty.
detailWindow.example: How often your check-ins said it was working, by hours after logging. The shaded band is how sure the app is.

detailEstimates.context: Explains the estimates chart: your guess, then what it really took; plans add a buffer.
detailEstimates.example: Your guess, then what it actually took. Plans now add the difference for you.

detailSleep.context: Explains the sleep chart: bars are hours slept, the line is how much of the plan got done the next day.
detailSleep.example: Bars are hours slept. The line is how much of the next day’s plan got done.

detailLogs.context: Explains the log-times chart: each dot a logged morning; the band is where most fall.
detailLogs.example: Each dot is a logged morning. The band is where most of them land.

dayTypesIntro.context: Intro to day types on the Medication page: different days have different rhythms; name them anything.
dayTypesIntro.example: Different days, different rhythms. Name them whatever makes sense to you.

dayTypesLimit.context: They hit the free plan’s three day types; Plus has unlimited. No pressure wording.
dayTypesLimit.example: The free plan holds three day types. Plus holds as many as your life has.

actionButtonPitch.context: Suggestion right after medication setup: log with one press of the Action button.
actionButtonPitch.example: Want to log with one press? Your Action button can do it.

personaliseIntro.context: Intro to the Personalise page: tell us when you like doing things and the plan leans that way.
personaliseIntro.example: Tell us when you like doing things. The plan will lean that way.

categoriesLimit.context: They hit the free plan’s five categories; Plus has unlimited.
categoriesLimit.example: Five categories on the free plan. Plus if you need more boxes. We won’t judge.

socialIntro.context: Explains social suggestions: the phone spots plans with people and suggests better times; nothing is ever sent for them.
socialIntro.example: Your phone can spot plans with people and suggest better times. Nothing ever gets sent for you.

hyperfixationWarning.context: Quirky warning at the top of the Customise page: this might become their hyperfixation and eat the next six hours.
hyperfixationWarning.example: Careful. This page might become your hyperfixation and eat the next six hours.

customiseIntro.context: Intro to Customise: make it yours; nothing here can break your plan.
customiseIntro.example: Make it yours. Nothing here can break your plan.

focusDoneCheer.context: Small cheer after marking a focus block done.

fixHeadline.context: Fix my day headline: count small changes (count is 2 or more).

fixSubtitle.context: Fix my day subtitle: running minutes over; this is the smallest change that keeps today on track.
fixSubtitle.example: You’re running {minutes} min over. Here’s the smallest change that keeps today on track.
